advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the env-registry generator so `(alias resolver)` provenance is only added for aliases actually in config.py::_LEGACY_ENV_ALIASES (i.e. permanent renames), not for scheduled/superseded env entries like REBAR_LLM_MODEL, then regenerate docs/env-vars.md.
evidence: scripts/gen_env_registry.py:150-155 unconditionally unions `src/rebar/config.py (alias resolver)` for all env aliases: `for alias_name in aliases: reads.setdefault(alias_name, set()).add("src/rebar/config.py (alias resolver)")`
gen_env_registry.py:132-145 `_env_aliases()` iterates ALL env-kind REGISTRY entries (permanent and scheduled) with no filter for whether they are in _LEGACY_ENV_ALIASES
_config_sources.py:295-311 `_LEGACY_ENV_ALIASES` contains only the six permanent renames; REBAR_LLM_MODEL is absent
Ticket comment (verified): 'there is NO alias-resolver path — neither src/rebar/config.py nor _config_schema.py mentions the var, so _LEGACY_ENV_ALIASES is not involved'
advisory.finding: The generated docs/env-vars.md falsely attributes REBAR_LLM_MODEL to `src/rebar/config.py (alias resolver)`. The env-registry generator adds that provenance to every env-kind REGISTRY entry, but REBAR_LLM_MODEL is a _scheduled supersession that is NOT in config.py's _LEGACY_ENV_ALIASES and is never resolved through the config alias resolver — it is read only in llm/config.py and llm/model_classes.py.
advisory.suggested_fix: In scripts/gen_env_registry.py, gate the `(alias resolver)` union on membership in rebar._config_sources._LEGACY_ENV_ALIASES rather than on presence in the deprecation REGISTRY, so a scheduled/superseded env var without a config-alias resolver keeps only its real os.environ.get read sites.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a config-table `model` on one class slot wins over a set REBAR_LLM_MODEL (config table > bare var), while an unset class still receives the fan-out.
evidence: test_explicit_class_config_beats_the_deprecated_var sets `REBAR_LLM_STANDARD_MODEL` (an env override applied at line 164, `_env_override`), not a config-table `model` key (line 156)
docs/llm-example-configs.md: 'Resolution order, per field: ... > the config table > the deprecated bare `REBAR_LLM_MODEL` > the built-in default'
ABSENCE: no test passes `parse_class_slots({'standard': {'model': ...}})` with REBAR_LLM_MODEL set to assert the config-table value wins
advisory.finding: The documented precedence rung 'config table > bare REBAR_LLM_MODEL' is untested: no test supplies a config-table `model` for a class and asserts it beats the fan-out. test_explicit_class_config_beats_the_deprecated_var exercises the per-class ENV layer (_parse_slot line 164) not the config-table layer (line 156), so a refactor swapping `raw.get('model') or fallback_default` to `fallback_default or raw.get('model')` on line 156 would invert this rung with the whole suite still green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add: set REBAR_LLM_MODEL=X; call parse_class_slots({'standard': {'model': 'Y'}}); assert slots['standard'].model == 'Y' and slots['frontier'].model == 'X'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the comment-substring grep with the behavioral registry assertion already present, or drop it as a change-detector on comment prose.
evidence: `assert "holds ONLY these permanent" not in src...`
The grepped tokens live in a `#` block comment (_deprecations.py:75-96), not a contract any parser/registry/generator consumes
advisory.finding: test_the_registry_comment_no_longer_claims_permanent_only asserts against SOURCE-CODE COMMENT prose in _deprecations.py (substring 'holds ONLY these permanent' absent; 'supersession|superseded' present). This is source-grepping of a non-executable comment with no non-human consumer — a change-detector that breaks on any behavior-preserving rewording of the comment rather than verifying observable behavior.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] For the argparse `--help` and MCP tool-description surfaces, assert on the RENDERED output (parser.format_help() / the tool descriptor) rather than grepping the module source.
evidence: `text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"); if "provider per REBAR_LLM_MODEL" in text:`
The docstring names it 'these RENDER' — but the test reads the module source, not the rendered `--help` output or the MCP tool descriptor
advisory.finding: test_the_rendered_operator_facing_strings_no_longer_advertise_the_var greps the SOURCE text of _llm_commands.py / _mcp_llm.py / config.py for description/docstring substrings ('provider per REBAR_LLM_MODEL', 'model id (default') rather than exercising the rendered surface (argparse `format_help()`, the MCP tool description). It asserts implementation text, not observable output, and breaks on a behavior-preserving reword.
